chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Wahb ibn Abd Rabbihi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever says, 'Allah knows' what he does not know, His Throne shakes due to that, in magnification for Him.

key_terms.إِعْظَاماً: In magnification/glorification — expressing reverence for God's greatness
key_terms.اللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ: Allah knows — the affirmation of divine omniscience
key_terms.اهْتَزَّ عَرْشُهُ: His Throne shakes — a cosmic response signifying divine majesty

ai.seo_question: What happens when one says 'Allah knows' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that divine knowledge is absolute and without limitation. The act of attributing to God knowledge of what a human does not know — effectively affirming God's omniscience while acknowledging one's own ignorance — is so profound a recognition of divine majesty that even the Throne of God trembles in glorification. This hadith was transmitted in the context of emphasizing proper theological humility: when confronted with matters beyond human comprehension, acknowledging God's all-encompassing knowledge is itself an act of reverence.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Wahab Bin Abd Rabbihi, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘The one who says, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Knows’, what he does not know, His<sup>azwj</sup> Throne shakes due to that, in Magnification for Him<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Wahab ibn ‘Abd Rabbihi who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one says, “Allah knows”, when he does not know something, the Throne of Allah vibrates as a sign of expressing His greatness.”’
